title: Gill's India, Sans Pant and Shami: BCCI's Afghanistan Squads Signal a Generational Shift
excerpt: Bumrah rested, Pant dropped from ODIs and stripped of vice-captaincy, Shami not even discussed — the selectors are building for 2027 and beyond
body:
Shubman Gill will captain India in both the one-off Test and three-match ODI series against Afghanistan this June — the same month that could begin to define who plays at the 2027 ODI World Cup and who watches from home. The squads announced by the BCCI on Monday carry messages that extend well beyond a bilateral assignment against the 13th-ranked team in the world.

The Omissions Say More Than the Inclusions

Start with the names that are not on either list.

Jasprit Bumrah, India's most valuable cricketing asset, has been rested for the entire series. Chief selector Ajit Agarkar framed it as workload management — Bumrah bowled through a demanding IPL 2026 campaign for Mumbai Indians, and India's packed calendar stretches deep into the year with the Border-Gavaskar Trophy and an England tour on the horizon. No one disputes the logic: Bumrah at 80 per cent in October is worth more than Bumrah at full tilt in June. But for the first time in years, India will play a home series without even having him in reserve.

Mohammed Shami is nowhere. Not in the Test squad where his 2025-26 Ranji Trophy numbers screamed for selection, and not in the ODIs where his IPL form for Lucknow Super Giants has been steady if unspectacular. Agarkar's explanation was bracingly blunt: "There was no discussion regarding him." Five words that likely end Shami's international career in all but the official retirement announcement. The man who bowled India to the 2023 World Cup final appears to have been simply left behind by time and a new selection regime.

Rishabh Pant remains in the Test squad, but loses the vice-captaincy to KL Rahul — a demotion that follows his removal from the ODI squad altogether. After a miserable IPL 2026 campaign with Lucknow Super Giants that included a very public F-bomb on live television, Pant's white-ball regression has forced the selectors' hand. Shreyas Iyer takes the ODI vice-captaincy instead.

The New Guard Steps Forward

The names that have earned call-ups tell the more interesting story.

Prince Yadav, the LSG left-arm quick who received his maiden India ODI call-up on the same evening Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashed him around Jaipur, represents the selectors' willingness to look past a single bad night. Yadav's IPL 2026 numbers — pace, movement, and the nerve to bowl at the death — have been persuasive enough to survive the mauling.

Ishan Kishan returns to the ODI fold after his match-winning 70 off 47 balls steered Sunrisers Hyderabad into the IPL playoffs just 24 hours earlier. Kishan's exile from international cricket, which began after the 2024 South Africa tour, appears to be decisively over.

Gurnoor Brar and Manav Suthar earn Test squad inclusions, a signal that India's next generation of spin-bowling all-rounders is being actively auditioned. Ravindra Jadeja has been rested, and with his 38th birthday approaching, the selectors are clearly planning for a world without him.

The Squads

Test (June 6-10, Mullanpur): Shubman Gill (c), Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul (vc), Sai Sudharsan, Rishabh Pant, Devdutt Padikkal, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Manav Suthar, Harpreet Brar, Dhruv Jurel.

ODIs (June 14 Dharamsala, June 17 Lucknow, June 20 Chennai): Shubman Gill (c), Shreyas Iyer (vc), Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, KL Rahul (wk), Ishan Kishan (wk), Hardik Pandya, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Washington Sundar, Harsh Dubey, Kuldeep Yadav, Arshdeep Singh, Prasidh Krishna, Prince Yadav, Gurnoor Brar.

Rohit Sharma and Hardik Pandya's inclusion in the ODI squad remains subject to fitness clearance — both missed IPL matches with injuries in recent weeks.

What NRIs Should Know

The one-off Test begins June 6 at the new MYS International Cricket Stadium in Mullanpur (New Chandigarh), a venue making its international debut. The ODIs follow in Dharamsala (June 14), Lucknow (June 17), and Chennai (June 20) — all evening starts in India, which means morning viewing in North America and afternoon slots in the UK.

For the diaspora, the ODI squad is the one that matters most: Rohit and Kohli are both in it, making these among the last opportunities to watch the two veterans in tandem before the 2027 World Cup cycle narrows further. JioHotstar carries live coverage in India, with Willow TV and FanCode servicing North American and international audiences respectively.

The 2027 Roadmap

Agarkar and the BCCI have been explicit: this Afghanistan series is not a standalone event. It is a checkpoint on the road to the 2027 ODI World Cup in Southern Africa and the World Test Championship. The decisions made here — resting Bumrah, promoting Gill as the long-term leader, building around young IPL performers, and moving past fading stars — are the first pages of a longer document.

The message to every cricketer who did not make these squads is equally clear: the door is not locked, but the selectors have found new keys.
